Hawks Under fire

By: Bernadette Maguire | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Top Hawks officials face the axe - we bring you the intriguing lowdown on alleged coverups, allegations of political interference and ask - how does this impact on the administration of justice?

Summary:
You can't ignore the fact that the Hawks like their predecessors the Scorpions aren't in line to win any popularity contests. Dale Carnegie isn't even in their sights.

But high ranking Hawks officials certainly have felt the brunt of what's alleged to be a purging of officials who took their jobs of corruption busting too seriously.

KZN's Booysen was the first casualty accused of running a death squad after he set up a sting operation to net an ANC stalwart who had siphoned off millions...then came General Dramat - suspended in December on rendition charges dating back 5 years that we have been reliably informed, he was exonerated of any wrongdoing by Robert McBride of IPID and who has agreed to testify. And now this week Gauteng Hawks boss, General Shadrack Sibiya was also implicated. We believe that tomorrow another top Hawks official will join their ranks.



Further information:
Rumours abound as to what is behind the string of suspensions...some say Dramat had called for the Nkandla file and was planning an investigation, others argue that the UN asked for the rendition charges to be re-opened, some say it is to do with political interference by Phiyega who holds the purse strings and is trying to keep control and order over a unit who gets too close to No 1 too often. Some say Mdluli is skulking in the shadows...

Our job will be to shift through the smoke and mirrors and ask some tough questions - what is going on, where is the independence of the Hawks and what impact will the current situation have on the administration of justice?

Press Release:


Hawks bosses suspended
While speculation is still rife over the actual circumstances behind the recent suspension of top Hawks officials, these events serve as a chilling reminder of the Scorpions’ disbandment in 2008. Could this all be an attempt to divert attention from sensitive, high-level investigations? Carte Blanche asks what the alleged political interference linked to these events may mean for the administration of justice.


Script:


Visuals Script

13 October 2013


VO: 19
Apparently damning documents surface placing Hawks boss Lieutenant general Anwa Dramat at the centre of rendition scandal in which 4 Zimbabweans allegedly arrested in South Africa are sent across the border to be tortured and killed in a case dating back to November 2010.

The Hawks retaliate saying it’s a dirty tricks campaign aimed at discrediting Dramat.

18 October 2013

Dramat is sent an email by Police minister Nathi Nthleko cautioning him of his imminent suspension.

9 December 2014

Dramat is summonsed from his seaside holiday during the festive season and flown to Pretoria to meet the minister and in the presence of police commissioner Riah Phiyega – he is handed a letter, a letter placing him on cautionary suspension for 60 days. Helen Suzman Foundation director Francis Antonie finds the circumstances suspicious.

23 December 2014

Francis:
Why did this all emerge literally on Christmas eve, when everyone is on holiday? Why this delay from 2010, to 2013 to 2014 and now it’s 2015.


John link: 35:22
Then last week 2 more high profile officials arrests Shadrack Sibiya and Leslie Maluleke were also suspended. The move fuelled allegations of a politically inspired purge aimed at clipping the Hawks wings.

VO: 6”
On Wednesday this week Hawks spokesman Captain Paul Ramaloko, who this week was moved to the national office, defended the high level suspensions.

Paul:
We are talking about a deportation of wanted suspects in Zimbabwe which was done by our members which has some questions in terms of procedural fairness.


VO: 33”
But it’s now surfacing that the rendition story may simply be a smoke screen and the charges spurious. In a leaked letter Dramat claims that political interference is to blame. Author Prince Mashile who served as a technical expert when the Hawks were set up says he isn’t surprised by the ruse claims.

Prince:
So if you are investigating the president who ultimately is the person who accept all the appointments, surely then the president has the power to remove you out of his way.

VO:
Dramat claims the tipping point came when he requested SAPS files for an investigation into Jacob Zuma’s 246 million rand Nkandla homestead. Other high profile investigations that didn’t win him any points in the popularity stakes include a probe into ANC northern cape leader John Block and a 60 million rand fraud case involving Thoshan Panday – an associate of the president’s son. The DA’s shadow minister for police, Dianne Kohler-Barnard is convinced that its all about protecting no 1.

Diane:
Anwa Dramat as the head of the Hawks has legally the right to call up any investigation and to pull it under the wing of the Hawks and to conduct that investigation without fear or favour and he called for the Nkandla file.

VO:
The Panday investigation is also widely believed to have been the driving force in the public arrest and humiliation of KZN Hawks boss – Major General Johan Booysen who was accused on trumped up charges of running a death squad. Booysen has since been vindicated, re-instated and recently obtained an urgent interdict preventing the police commissioner from firing him.


VO: 14
Hugh Glenister who to date has spent 6 million rand on court cases, initially on fighting the disbandment of the Scorpions and more recently fighting for the independence of the Hawks believes the police minister is insulting public intelligence.


Hugh:
Do the politicians think that the South African population are dumb or stupid, they believe they are the king, they can do what they want and that’s not what democracy is about.


John:
What’s your response to the allegations that there was a request for a handover of the Nkandla and that General Dramat refused?

Paul:
I would also not like to get to that but I know for a fact that investigations on Nkandla are conducted by the National investigating unit led by Lt-General Moonoo.

VO:
Adding to the intrigue a source close to the investigation has told us that IPID boss Robert McBride is willing to testify that Dramat and Sibiya were cleared in his investigation.

Prince:
So if he was exonerated for the rendition thing why is it brought up again? Quite clearly there is a bigger motive.

VO: 8”

It also flies in the face of a hard won Suzman foundation constitutional court judgement around the independence of the Hawks delivered in November. The court ruled that the minister may not axe a hawks boss without following due process.

Francis:
The court has ruled, it’s made the piece of legislation constitutionally compliant and that’s why the minister’s intervention here is so apparently at odds with what we understand the constitutional court is about.

Diane:
If the constitutional court judges say that he is in contempt of our ruling, go and arrest him, who will do that?

John:
Let’s talk about how the Hawks are going to respond to this… Are you prepared to fight the ministry on this?

Paul R:
We respect the action taken by the Minister, and whatever the minister did should be responded to by his office.


SAPS link John:
We requested interviews with the national police minister as well as the Commissioner of police but sadly we were stonewalled. Not even their spokespeople are allowed to talk to us, that’s despite the fact that on an issue as important as this one surely the South African public deserves an explanation.

Hugh:
It’s shocking. These are members who have been put there by the citizenry.. We have all the rights to know. When the state forgets that they are our servants and they think they are our masters you are one step closer to tyranny.

VO: 12”
Given these recent events, its little wonder that parallels are being drawn with the disbandment of the Scorpions and the fate of Advocate Vusi Pikoli, who found himself axed on what he calls concocted charges.

Hugh:
Scopa gets taken out, then the Scorpions, and now the Hawks, so the direction is obvious. We don’t want oversight. The direction of society should be that we want more oversight because the more power you have the more oversight we require.

VO: 7”
And while NGOs and opposition parties are sounding off, the ANC and political leaders have remained silent on the issue.

Hugh:
The moral indignation is not there coming from the ANC and not coming from the leadership, so I don’t suspect one individual - this is a 'I scratch your back you scratch my back' kind of relationship.

Prince:
Without Zuma they would not be Ministers, so that’s what we need to understand. The people in the ANC act the way they do because their personal survival is linked to the Zuma project.


John link:
It appears the Hawks aren’t the only state agency undergoing an alleged purge; the South African revenue service is also experiencing a major and controversial shake-up.

VO: 14
Deputy commissioner Ivan Pillay has been suspended after allegations surfaced that he was running a rogue unit spying on political.... Diane says it has more to do with home improvements at Nkandla.

Diane:
Of course you have to pay tax. You can’t simply take 230 million. And someone dared to mention that and that person has been under attack ever since.

Prince:
Even there at SARS the name of Jacob Zuma comes up.

John link:
So why should ordinary South Africans care about what is happening at the Hawks? Well if an organization tasked with fighting corruption and organized crime succumbs to political interference we risk becoming a criminal state.

Hugh:
The big thing that scares me is that we actually have criminal syndicates involved with different politicians. So in other words, the syndication of the state, fighting for power, fighting for control, and general criminology that has overtaken us as a society.

VO: 3”
The Hawks spokesman says we’re jumping the gun.

Paul:
Nothing untoward about these actions that the employer is taking against these members of the Hawks. It is imperative that questions are answered surrounding the issue of renditions and it will come to finality, and work will continue.

VO: 6
Hugh’s not taking any chances... he’s putting his money where his mouth is.

Hugh:
What I’m going to do now - I’m putting a million rand fund together, which will fund the Institute for Accountability, the Free Market Foundation and the Suzman Foundation because I believe society now need some champions.

VO: 10”
On Friday the Suzman Foundation got to work and launched an urgent application to set aside the suspension order by the minister to be heard next week.

Francis:
We’re in for the long hau... this is the struggle and the struggle continues just by a different means.




Promo 1:

VO: 8”
Top Hawks officials face the axe - we bring you the intriguing lowdown on alleged cover-ups and allegations of political interference.

Hugh:
Name of Jacob Zuma comes up…


Promo 2:

VO:
Activists and NGOs aren’t buying the police’s official line on an alleged purging at the elite Hawks task team.

Prince:
So if you are investigating the president… out of his way.


Promo 3:

VO:
Top Hawks officials suspended, fighting for their careers – in a series of events which has raised the spectre of the Scorpions. Were they getting too close to the Zuma project?







VO: 4”'
Intelligence Hugh has gathered suggests its been brewing for months.

Hugh:
Their mandates have been taken away…budgets…they are pushed aside.




VO 8”
And Zimbabwean human rights lawyer and chairman of the Exiles Forum, Gabriel Shumba, welcomed the arrests.

Gabriel:
Not only does South Africa have an obligation….have seen several people dead.
